China AI-Driven Drug Discovery
Drug Discovery Riding the Next Wave of AI; initiate on Insilico & XtalPi at OW

We initiate coverage of two China AI-driven drug discovery (AIDD) companies, Insilico (3696.HK) and XtalPi (2228.HK), with Overweight (OW) ratings. China's AIDD sector is shifting from business exploration to early commercialization, supported by rising business development (BD) activities and clinical catalysts. Our positive view on China AIDD rests on three pillars: 1) AIDD has materially improved drug R&D productivity and could further increase success probability through “dry-wet lab” closed loop platforms; 2) AIDD coupled with China's structural cost and R&D pace and regulatory advantages could make China a more attractive hotbed for applying AIDD compared to overseas; and 3) The above factors have driven Big Pharma deal flow, clinical milestones, and significant topline growth, providing early validation for AIDD companies. We see a multi-year rerating opportunity, with Insilico and XtalPi offering complementary investment theses. We like Insilico for its high-risk, high reward pipeline built through AIDD and like XtalPi for its diverse businesses led by AIDD services and robotics wet lab. We rate both Insilico and XtalPi OW with PTs of HK$71 and HK$10, respectively.

- AIDD enables a measurable drug R&D unit-economics shift and provides real clinical promise to improve drug success probability. Closed-loop “dry lab + automated wet lab” platforms move discovery from trial-and-error to iterative, data-recycling execution that compounds a proprietary data flywheel, reducing early drug discovery cost and boosting efficiency. Beyond small molecule and antibody drugs, AIDD is capable of tackling complex and novel drug modalities. In addition, AI platforms are increasingly being integrated into clinical and regulatory workflows to de-risk late-stage drug development.

- AIDD players based in China are structurally better positioned than some overseas peers because of easy access to China's dense R&D infrastructure, which helps convert AIDD predictions into validated assets faster and more cheaply than overseas alternatives, anchoring the sector's structural cost advantage. Regulatory tailwinds are accelerating AIDD execution in China, as the NMPA shortens review timelines and builds AI-specific frameworks that lower the friction of moving candidates into human testing. Importantly, the proprietary data, including real-world clinical data from public hospitals in China, allow AIDD companies to leverage high-quality biological, pharmaceutical, and clinical data across many sources.

- Recent AIDD commercialization through services and BD, plus clinical catalysts, makes the timing to invest in AIDD to be now. Landmark BD deals with global Big Pharma provide multi-billion-dollar validation, while early-stage asset monetization turns cash-burning biotechs into non-dilutive revenue engines. AIDD continues to revolutionize drug discovery and development
Ever expanding AIDD market

The China AIDD sector is decisively transitioning from algorithmic promise to industrial execution. We think the core investment thesis rests on: 1) A paradigm shift in R&D unit economics, driven by powerful AIDD platforms/tools. More importantly, such AIDD platforms are becoming stronger because of closed-loop "dry-wet" lab systems (Pillar 1); 2) AIDD is uniquely anchored by China's unmatched supply chain density in drug R&D (Pillar 2); and 3) AIDD continues to be validated as de-risked by Big Pharma milestone capital (Pillar 3).

- The AIDD sector targets a rapidly expanding market ecosystem, with core AI-empowered pharmaceutical R&D spending to thrive, alongside a substantially broader generative AI opportunity. Driven by the pharmaceutical industry's urgent need to compress drug development cycles, lower costs and discover biologically sound new targets, global spending on AI-empowered drug R&D is forecast by F&S to grow at a 22.6% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) from US$11.9 billion in 2023 to US$74.6 billion by 2032. Furthermore, this sector is supported by the broader global generative AI market, which, according to F&S, is expanding at a 25.8% CAGR to reach a notable US$37.4 trillion by 2032. This vast technological expansion not only provides the foundational infrastructure for pharmaceutical platforms but also enables highly lucrative cross-sector commercialization into adjacent markets like advanced materials and agriculture.

The future of AIDD platforms/tools lies in closed loop, underlying LLM, and agent use with strong pharmaceutical knowledge

The integration of AI across the pharmaceutical value chain has produced a distinct ecosystem of AIDD platforms and tools but we don't see a single winning AIDD platform yet. These tools fundamentally shift research from a trial-and-error physical paradigm to a predictive, data-driven methodology, addressing distinct bottlenecks ranging from initial biological target discovery to molecular design and clinical trial forecasting. Based on our observations, we think AIDD tooling has converged around three “stacks” that differ mainly in (i) what is treated as ground truth (physics/chemistry/biology vs. learned representations) and (ii) where AI is used (speed-up, surrogate modeling, or end-to-end generation/reasoning). 1) Physics/pharmacology/biology/physiology models with AI used to accelerate computation. These platforms keep classical mechanistic formalisms (molecular dynamics [MD], quantum mechanics, PK/PD models, systems biology) as the core, and add machine learning (ML) for speed, scoring, or parameterization. Typical use: virtual screening triage, faster free-energy approximations, improved scoring functions, or adaptive sampling in molecular dynamics. Examples include: Schrödinger-style docking/FEP workflows; OpenMM-based MD ecosystems with ML potentials/surrogates, and Simcyp physiologically based

These systems are used in medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, CMC, and literature/ patent corpora, sometimes connected to tools (search, ELNs, assay databases) for grounded answers. Typical use: hypothesis generation, SAR summarization, protocol drafting, target/indication landscape reviews, and decision support. Examples include domain-adapted LLM assistants built on top of general LLMs; chemistry-aware LLM toolchains that call retrosynthesis/property predictors; literature/patent copilots used by R&D teams. In addition, various agent systems are built on top of LLMs to further facilitate the use of all three classes of AIDD tools. Overall, the development of AIDD is moving toward hybrid stacks: domain knowledge such as physics for correctness, deep models for priors and speed, and LLMs for orchestration and human-facing reasoning.

The 3 Key Pillars of China's AIDD
Pillar 1: AIDD Could Constantly Improve R&D Efficiency via "Dry-Wet Lab" Closed Loop

"What can AI solve for drugs?" The core value proposition of AIDD is a step-change in R&D unit economics. Most importantly, the "dry-wet lab" closed loops (AI + automation + wet-lab execution) utilized by major AIDD players in China are substantially compressing discovery timelines and lowering capital burn in drug discovery processes. The "dry lab" utilizes generative AI to virtually design molecules and predict their biological properties. These digital predictions are then sent directly to the "web lab" – a highly automated physical laboratory equipped with intelligent robotics - which rapidly synthesizes the compounds and tests them in the real world. The resulting experimental data is fed back into the dry lab to validate the initial prediction, effectively retraining the AI models to become smarter for the next round of drug design.

Still, the trajectory is encouraging: in AI-driven materials science, physics-based modelling and autonomous "self-driving" labs aim to compress discovery from 10–20 years to just 1–2 — screening battery-electrolyte chemistries down to a tested shortlist via active learning and accelerating perovskite solar-cell design through robotic synthesis. - AIDD Model generalization risk. A May 2026 Nature Structural & Molecular Biology study (Škrinjar et al.) exposed a key weakness in the AI tools that predict how a drug molecule fits into a protein—the core task behind AI drug discovery. The researchers tested leading models (AlphaFold3, Chai-1, Boltz-1, Protenix) on 2,600 protein–ligand structures the models had never seen during training. On familiar cases, accuracy was about 70%; on genuinely new ones, it collapsed to single digits (AlphaFold3 ~9%, Boltz-1 ~5%). In plain terms, the AI was largely copying answers it had memorized rather than truly figuring out where new molecules bind—and it couldn’t tell when it was wrong, since its confidence scores had almost no link to actual accuracy. Adding more training data (Boltz-2 vs. Boltz-1) did not help. Because drug discovery is fundamentally about brand-new, uncharted targets, this challenges the “structure prediction is solved” narrative and favors platforms that pair AI with physics-based validation to double-check predictions.

Following a positive Phase IIa readout, the program has advanced into the pivotal Phase III GENESIS-IPF-3 trial in China, initiated in July 2026, with topline data expected around 2029 per company data.

- IPF remains a high-need and underserved market, with only three drugs approved globally as of July 2026: Pirfenidone (Esbriet, Roche), Nintedanib (OFEV, Boehringer Ingelheim), Nerandomilast (Jascayd, Boehringer Ingelheim PDE4B inhibitor; FDA approval in October 2025). Nintedanib generics are expected to enter China in 2026. Existing therapies primarily slow disease progression and are associated with tolerability limitations, while several high-profile candidates, including pamrevlumab, bexotegrast, and GLPG1690, have failed in development. Rentosertib's novel oral, first-in-class TNIK mechanism is differentiated from the crowded TGF-\( \beta \)/kinase landscape. By simultaneously modulating the Wnt, TGF-\( \beta \), and NF-\( \kappa \) B pathways, the drug benefits from both Breakthrough Therapy Designation and FDA Orphan Drug Designation, creating a meaningful competitive advantage.

Our PT of HK$71 is derived from SOTP

We value Insilico Medicine (3696.HK) on a sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) basis. As a pipeline-deep AIDD company, its valuation is largely anchored by its collaboration revenue, with AI service streams as a secondary contributor. Our analysis yields HK$71 per share. The key to Insilico's premium lies in demonstrated clinical validation—superior success rates and predictive accuracy, allowing us to justify a higher pipeline probability of success (PoS) versus traditional biotech.

- Pipeline-led value shifts focus to clinical probabilities over platform multiples. The collaboration revenue accounts for about ~US$4.4bn of its total EV of ~US5bn, making the PoS assumption the primary driver of valuation. This dynamic is structurally different from breadth-first platforms like XTalPi, where it has meaningful amount of service businesses. Here, valuation is more sensitive to clinical readouts, particularly a few lead assets.

- Premium is supported by differentiated clinical-outcome evidence.
Insilico reports Phase I success rates of 80–90% versus a traditional 40–65% baseline, and Phase I-to-approval probability of 9–18% versus 5–10% historically. This suggests that the platform enhances probability of success, not just development speed—an important distinction underpinning our premium thesis and one that is difficult for peers to replicate.

- Predictive-accuracy metrics provide auditable support for the premium. The company discloses measurable benchmarks, including 0.86 AUC-ROC for Phase II outcome prediction (inClinico), ~84% protein-folding accuracy, and ~75% toxicity-prediction accuracy. These quantitative indicators serve as evidence that Insilico's AI confers a real, reproducible edge beyond narrative positioning. We apply a uniform PoS uplift of 15% (vs XAIPI's 10%) to reflect improved clinical probabilities.

We rate Insilico Medicine at Overweight as the novel-target, pipeline-led way to gain exposure to China's AI drug discovery theme. Its repeatable out-licensing model provides a scalable monetization engine, generating upfront payments, milestones and future royalties while funding continued pipeline expansion. With multiple clinical readouts, business development opportunities and new platform initiatives expected over 2026–2027, we see a rich catalyst path that offers significant upside, albeit with higher clinical and execution risk than service-led peers given its greater dependence on proprietary pipeline success.
